premise: You moved to Granada and you live there. There is no plot. There are districts, and everything that happens to somebody living in a Nicaraguan city. Winning is doing all of it.
open_world: OPEN WORLD. Nothing is locked. You can walk into any district on the first day and talk to anybody. Tier is a difficulty label for authoring order and for what the game SUGGESTS next - it is never a gate. If a player wants to walk into a tier-five conversation on day one and lose it, that is their business.
no_puzzles: This is a language game, not a Zelda game. A mission must never be a puzzle you have to think your way through. Being lost is a nudge, not a maze: ask somebody, get pointed, go. The difficulty lives in the Spanish, nowhere else.

centro.name: El Centro
centro.desc: Parque Central, la catedral, La Calzada. Where the tourists are, and where people would rather practise their English on you.

mercado.name: El Mercado
mercado.desc: The municipal market and the streets around it. Loud, cheap, and where you learn what things actually cost.

xalteva.name: Xalteva
xalteva.desc: The old quarter west of the centre. Churches, quiet streets, old people with time to talk.

guadalupe.name: Guadalupe
guadalupe.desc: East, sloping toward the water. Families, workshops, kids in the street.

pantanal.name: Pantanal
pantanal.desc: Down by the lake. Poorer, wetter, the part of Granada no postcard shows.

malecon.name: El Malecón
malecon.desc: The lakefront. Boats, fried fish, Sunday crowds.

terminal.name: La Terminal
terminal.desc: Buses in and out. Everyone here is going somewhere or has just arrived.

barrio.name: Tu barrio
barrio.desc: Your own street. The landlady, the pulpería on the corner, neighbours who hear everything.

trabajo.name: El trabajo
trabajo.desc: The workshop and the errands that pay. Where your Spanish stops being polite and starts being useful.

tramites.name: Trámites y salud
tramites.desc: Offices, clinics, queues. The Spanish nobody teaches and everybody needs.

fiestas.name: Las fiestas
fiestas.desc: The calendar. Some come round once a year and you will miss one.

afuera.name: Afuera
afuera.desc: Masaya, Catarina, la Laguna, Mombacho. You need wheels and a reason.

crowd.note: Sells something from a doorway. Knows who buys what.
Kids on bikes. Know where everyone is, and are wrong about a third of the time.
Out in a rocking chair. Sees everything on the street.
Waiting for a fare. Knows every address in town.
Working on something. Short answers, useful ones.
Has time. Tells you more than you asked.
Lost, and speaks English at you. Talking to them raises your chele.
Watching parked motos. Sees who comes and goes.
Wants to invite you somewhere, and genuinely knows the barrio.
Answers what you ask and nothing more.
